title: Specialized Investment Funds (SIF) in India: A Complete Guide
description: Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) are a sophisticated investment vehicle in India, regulated by SEBI. They offer greater flexibility in investment strategie.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF)?
faq.a: The minimum investment for most SIFs (which fall under AIFs) is typically ₹1 crore. For some categories or specific investor types, this might be higher.

faq.q: Are SIFs the same as mutual funds?
faq.a: No, SIFs are distinct from mutual funds. SIFs have greater flexibility in investment strategies and asset classes, higher minimum investment, and are generally less liquid than mutual funds.

faq.q: Who regulates Specialized Investment Funds in India?
faq.a: Specialized Investment Funds (as AIFs) are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.

faq.q: What kind of assets do SIFs invest in?
faq.a: SIFs can invest in a wide range of assets including unlisted equities, private equity, venture capital, real estate, infrastructure projects, distressed assets, and complex derivatives.

faq.q: What are the main risks associated with SIFs?
faq.a: The main risks include lower liquidity (due to lock-in periods), higher investment risk (due to complex strategies and illiquid assets), and potential for capital loss.

faq.q: How is income from SIFs taxed in India?
faq.a: Taxation is complex and depends on the AIF category. Category I and II AIFs often have a pass-through status for certain income, while Category III AIFs may be taxed at the fund level. It is advisable to consult a tax expert.
